To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the average accretion rates of protostars during their embedded phase are nearly constant, with the Class 0 and early Class I sources accreting at rates similar to those observed in T Tauri stars, and (2) the average lifetime of the Class I phase is ~10^5 yr.

the average Class 0 lifetime is 1.7 × 10^6 yr, that Class 0 sources accrete at an average rate of 2 × 10^(–4) M_☖ yr^(–1), that Class I sources accrete at rates of 2-3 × 10^(6) yr, and that accretion is episodic in both classes.
We have identified 128 deeply embedded protostellar candidates, including 39 Class 00/I sources in Perseus and 50 Class 0/I sources in Serpens.

the Class 0 and early Class I phases are characterized by nearly constant accretion rate, but the later Class I phase has episodic accretions.

there is a large spread in accretion rate at each stage of the protostellar evolutionary sequence.
